request.message: Which rivers drain the western side of the primary watershed in the area around Holmfirth and Glossop?

response.answer: On the western side of the primary watershed, the drainage is to the Mersey by the rivers Tame and Etherow; the basin of the Etherow forms a salient projecting some seven miles east of the general run of the North Sea—Irish Sea divide [E2].

evidences.doc_title: The Geology of the Country Around Holmfirth and Glossop (excerpt)
section_path: THE GEOLOGY OF THE COUNTRY AROUND
evidences.text:
On the western side of this line the drainage is to the Mersey
by the rivers Tame and Etherow; the basin of the latter forms a
salient projecting some seven miles east of the general run of
the North Sea—Irish Sea divide (see map, Fig. 1). To the east
the drainage is to rivers entering the Humber; the Marsden
Brook and the Holme with their tributaries join the Calder; the
Dearne, Little Don and Ewden Beck all join the Don, of which
the main stream rises around Dunford Bridge and flows through
Penistone.

request.message: What are the most satisfactory arable crops grown in the soils of the Coal Measures?

response.answer: Wheat, oats and potatoes are perhaps the most satisfactory arable crops grown in the soils of the Coal Measures. [E1]

evidences.doc_title: The Geology of the Country Around Holmfirth and Glossop (excerpt)
evidences.text:
8 GEOLOGY OF HOLMFIRTH AND GLOSSOP :
The soils of the Coal Measures are on the whole better than
those of the Millstone Grits, though they suffer from the same
lack of lime. The shales often give a heavy clay soil, which is
mostly under grass, but the sandstones give lighter loams. Wheat,
oats and potatoes are perhaps the-most satisfactory arable crops;
swedes and turnips are apt to suffer from ‘ finger and toe ’ disease,
unless liming is liberal.'

request.message: Which device can be used to share one IP address among multiple computers?

response.answer: An AirPort Base Station can be used to share one IP address among multiple computers [E2]. A router capable of network address translation (NAT), also known as "IP masquerading," is also required to share a connection when only one IP address is provided [E1].

evidences.doc_title: MacBook Air User Guide (archival edition)
evidences.text:
If you have two or more computers sharing an Internet connection, be sure that your
wireless network is set up properly. You need to know if your ISP provides only one IP
address or if it provides multiple IP addresses, one for each computer.
If only one IP address is provided, then you must have a router capable of sharing the
connection, also known as network address translation (NAT) or “IP masquerading.”
For setup information, check the documentation provided with your router or ask the
person who set up your network.
